title: How to Ask for a Recommendation Letter: Emails and Preparation
content:
Choose a referee who knows your work well enough to give specific examples. Ask early, explain the application and provide a short information pack that helps them write an accurate recommendation.

Who should write your recommendation?

Choose someone who has directly assessed your academic work, research, employment or professional contributions and can give specific examples. A senior title is less important than an informed, credible recommendation. Confirm whether the programme requires academic rather than professional referees.

Ask early and make it easy to write an accurate letter

  1. Read how many referees are required and how submission works.
  2. Ask the potential referee if they can write a supportive, specific recommendation.
  3. State the programme or award and the exact deadline.
  4. Supply your CV, transcript, project details and the selection criteria.
  5. Send a respectful reminder before the deadline if needed, and thank them afterward.

Email template: asking a professor

Subject: Recommendation request for [programme] — deadline [date]

Dear Dr [Surname],

I took [course / research project] with you in [term/year], where I worked on [specific assignment or project]. I am applying to [exact programme] at [institution], and I wanted to ask whether you would feel comfortable writing a strong academic recommendation for me.

The submission deadline is [date, time and time zone], and the university sends referees a secure upload link. If you are able to help, I can send my CV, transcript, statement and a short summary of the work I completed with you.

Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
[Name]

Email template: asking an employer

Subject: Reference request for [degree/scholarship] — [date]

Dear [Name],

I am applying for [programme/award], which requests a professional reference. Since we worked together on [specific responsibility], I wondered if you would be comfortable commenting on [relevant skills supported by your observations].

The deadline is [date], and I can share the criteria and submission instructions. Please feel free to decline if you do not have sufficient time.

Kind regards,
[Name]

Polite reminder template

Subject: Gentle reminder — recommendation due [date]

Dear [Name],

Thank you again for agreeing to write my recommendation. The deadline for [programme] is [date and time zone]. I wanted to check whether you received the submission link and whether I can provide anything else useful.

Many thanks,
[Name]

What information should you provide?

ItemWhy it helps
CV and transcriptProvides dates, courses and achievements to verify
Programme and criteriaShows what the selection panel needs
Relevant project summaryRefreshes the referee’s memory of specific work
Submission link/instructionsAvoids portal errors
Deadline with time zonePrevents last-minute confusion

Avoid these mistakes

  • Writing a fictional letter for a referee to sign unless they specifically request an accurate draft and the rules permit it.
  • Requesting a reference on the deadline day.
  • Sending an undocumented list of exaggerated achievements.
  • Submitting a letter yourself when the programme requires direct referee submission.
  • Assuming every scholarship accepts professional references.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use the same referee for several applications?

Often yes, with their permission. Give a clear list of deadlines and programme requirements.

What if a referee declines?

Thank them and ask someone with direct knowledge of your work. It is better to receive a specific letter from an appropriate referee than a generic one from a famous person.

Official guidance and further reading

  • UCAS: postgraduate personal statements

Give your referee a manageable information pack

Send the programme name, deadline and submission instructions, together with your CV and a short reminder of work the referee supervised. Explain why you are applying and which relevant tasks they observed. If several applications are involved, put the dates in one clear table. Ask whether they can provide a supportive reference before listing their details. A suitable reminder might say: “The reference portal closes on [date]. Please let me know if you need any further material from me.” Do not write achievements on their behalf or ask them to confirm work they have not seen.
